title: Burst Capacity Metrics Taxonomy (Draft): Naming, Labels, Cardinality, Examples
content:
Context
- This doc defines draft metric naming conventions + label/cardinality constraints for Dedicated “burst capacity” telemetry.
- Intended to be used by: burst admission controller service, routing/gateway, fleet/pool controllers, and SRE dashboards/alerts.
- Primary goal: burst should be observable without causing Prometheus label explosions (tenant_id, request_id, model_name, etc.).

Non-goals
- This is not the full dashboard spec (see Grafana work in observability-pack/pr-612).
- This doc does not define billing-grade metering (those signals can share components but will have separate ingestion + reconciliation requirements).


1) Naming conventions
Metric namespace
- Prefix: redwood_burst_
- Prefer nouns for state (gauges) and verbs for events (counters).
- Units must be encoded in the metric name.

Type conventions
- Counter: *_total
- Gauge: no suffix (or *_ratio for [0..1])
- Histogram: *_seconds or *_tokens etc. Use Prometheus histogram conventions: _bucket/_sum/_count.

Examples
- redwood_burst_admission_requests_total (counter)
- redwood_burst_admission_decisions_total (counter)
- redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio (gauge)
- redwood_burst_admission_eval_duration_seconds (histogram)


2) Label policy (high-level)
Allowed labels (default)
- region: short region identifier (e.g., us-east, eu-west)
- hardware_class: enum-like (h100, a100, l40s) — do NOT include SKU variants unless they materially change behavior and are stable
- pool: stable pool identifier within region/hardware (e.g., “us-east-h100-burst-01”)
- decision: admitted | denied | queued | bypassed (bypassed = tenant not burst-enabled or request not eligible)
- reason: small bounded enum for denials/queues (see Reason codes section)
- tenant_tier: gold | silver | standard (or whatever Product defines; must be bounded)
- workload: interactive | batch (bounded; optional if routing has a stable classification)

Labels that are NOT allowed in Prometheus (ban list)
- tenant_id (raw) — too high cardinality
- customer_name
- request_id / trace_id
- model_name (unbounded; model churn creates long-lived label series)
- route_id / endpoint_path (can explode; use bounded “route_class” if needed)
- prompt_hash
- error_message

Notes
- If we must segment by tenant for debugging, we do it via:
  - Logs/traces with exemplars (trace_id) and/or
  - A separate low-QPS “debug metrics” endpoint gated to internal tooling, not scraped fleet-wide (see Support tooling PRs).


3) Cardinality budgets + constraints
Prometheus budget targets (per region)
- New time series introduced by burst should be < 25k per region (soft target) and < 50k per region (hard ceiling) at steady-state.
- Any metric with both “pool” and “reason” labels must keep “reason” to <= ~12 values.
- Any metric with “pool” must ensure pool names are stable (no embedding autoscaler instance ids).

Label value constraints
- reason must be a bounded enum (no free-form strings).
- pool names must be provisioned identifiers, not derived from k8s pod/node names.
- hardware_class must be normalized at ingestion (h100 not H100-SXM vs H100-PCIe unless we explicitly choose to split).
- region must match the platform region list (no cloud AZ labels).

Suggested “dimensionality tiers”
Tier 0 (always on)
- region, hardware_class
Tier 1 (allowed for fleet + SRE dashboards)
- + pool
Tier 2 (allowed for admission behavior)
- + decision, reason, tenant_tier
Tier 3 (debug only; not scraped globally)
- tenant_hash (if we do it at all) with strict sampling / allow-list


4) Reason codes (bounded enums)
Admission decision “reason” should be stable across services (admission controller, routing/gateway, console).

Proposed enums
- ok (only for decision=admitted; optional)
- not_eligible (request doesn’t qualify for burst; e.g., tenant not enabled)
- tenant_cap_reached (per-tenant burst cap)
- pool_capacity_exhausted (no burst capacity available in pool)
- fleet_safety_cap (global fleet safety cap triggered)
- cooldown_active (tenant is in cooldown window)
- fairness_throttle (token bucket / fairness model denied admission)
- telemetry_lag_protect (denied due to telemetry lag protection / smoothing guard)
- policy_override_disabled (burst disabled via kill-switch / config)
- admission_timeout (evaluation timed out; conservative deny)
- upstream_dependency_unhealthy (policy engine / telemetry dependency unhealthy)
- routing_fallback (routing decided not to attempt burst due to fallback policy)

Notes
- Keep the list short. Additions require observability + support review because dashboards/alerts need to interpret them.
- Avoid having separate “reason” enums per component; map component-specific codes into this set.


5) Core metrics: definitions + label sets
5.1 Admission controller
A) Requests into admission evaluation
- redwood_burst_admission_requests_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool, tenant_tier, workload
  - Semantics: increment when the admission controller receives an evaluation request (even if it short-circuits as not eligible)

B) Decision outcomes
- redwood_burst_admission_decisions_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool, tenant_tier, workload, decision, reason
  - Semantics: increment exactly once per admission evaluation.

C) Eval latency
- redwood_burst_admission_eval_duration_seconds
  - Type: histogram
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool
  - Buckets: 0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2
  - Semantics: wall-clock time to compute a decision.

D) Dependency health
- redwood_burst_admission_dependency_errors_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, dependency (telemetry|policy_engine|kv_store), error_class (timeout|5xx|decode|other)

E) Telemetry lag signal used by guardrails
- redwood_burst_telemetry_lag_seconds
  - Type: gauge
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool, source (fleet|scheduler|router)
  - Semantics: “freshness” of capacity/saturation signals at decision time.


5.2 Pool state (fleet / infra)
A) Pool utilization/saturation
- redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio
  - Type: gauge
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool
  - Semantics: burst_used_capacity / burst_total_capacity, where used is smoothed to avoid jitter.

- redwood_burst_pool_capacity_gpus
  - Type: gauge
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool, capacity_type (total|available|reserved_safety)

B) Queue / backlog (if queueing is supported)
- redwood_burst_pool_queue_depth
  - Type: gauge
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool

- redwood_burst_pool_queue_wait_seconds
  - Type: histogram
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool

C) Circuit breaker state
- redwood_burst_circuit_breaker_state
  - Type: gauge
  - Labels: region, scope (pool|fleet_global), hardware_class, pool
  - Values: 0=closed, 1=open

- redwood_burst_circuit_breaker_events_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, scope (pool|fleet_global), hardware_class, pool, event (opened|closed), trigger (slo_gate|fleet_safety|manual)


5.3 Routing / gateway integration
A) Attempts to use burst
- redwood_burst_routing_attempts_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, tenant_tier, workload
  - Semantics: routing attempted to request burst admission (before calling admission controller).

B) Admission call result
- redwood_burst_routing_admission_call_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, result (success|error|timeout)

C) Outcome at routing level
- redwood_burst_routing_outcomes_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, decision (admitted|denied|bypassed), reason
  - Note: reason should match the global enum set.

D) Fallback behavior
- redwood_burst_routing_fallbacks_total
  - Type: counter
  - Labels: region, fallback_type (queue|backpressure|alternate_pool|baseline_only|alternate_model), reason


5.4 Neighbor impact / protection signals (SRE-facing)
Goal: detect when burst activity causes tail latency regressions for non-burst tenants.

A) Non-burst SLO regression indicator
- redwood_burst_neighbor_latency_delta_seconds
  - Type: histogram (or gauge if we compute externally)
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool, percentile (p50|p95|p99), baseline_group (nonburst)
  - Semantics: observed_latency - reference_latency during comparable windows.

B) Tail amplification
- redwood_burst_tail_amplification_ratio
  - Type: gauge
  - Labels: region, hardware_class, pool
  - Semantics: p99_latency / p50_latency for non-burst traffic group.

C) SLO gate status
- redwood_burst_slo_gate_state
  - Type: gauge
  - Labels: region, gate (nonburst_latency|error_rate), state (enabled|disabled)
  - Values: 0=disabled, 1=enabled

Notes
- In practice, many of these are computed from existing request latency histograms in the gateway/runtime. The “burst” contribution is the extra grouping by pool/hardware_class and a dedicated dashboard panel to correlate with burst saturation and decisions.


6) Per-tenant visibility without high cardinality
We still need per-tenant dashboards for Console/CS, but Prometheus is the wrong storage for “tenant_id label everywhere.”

Recommended approach
- Prometheus: bounded labels only; provide fleet health, pool health, denial reasons by tier.
- Analytics/TSDB (internal): store per-tenant time series (tenant_id) for Console usage pages and CS reporting.
- Logs/Traces: per-request and per-tenant debugging; attach admission decision fields as structured attributes.

If a tenant dimension is required in metrics (strongly discouraged)
- Use tenant_bucket (e.g., hash(tenant_id) mod 64) as a last resort for distribution monitoring, not for attribution.
- Must be explicitly approved by Observability (Allison) + SRE (Sean) because it permanently increases series count.


7) Example PromQL queries (for dashboards)
Admission rate vs denial rate
- sum by (region, hardware_class, pool, reason) (rate(redwood_burst_admission_decisions_total{decision="denied"}[5m]))
- sum by (region, hardware_class, pool) (rate(redwood_burst_admission_decisions_total{decision="admitted"}[5m]))

Saturation panel
- avg by (region, hardware_class, pool) (redwood_burst_pool_saturation_ratio)

Telemetry lag alert candidate
- max by (region, hardware_class, pool) (redwood_burst_telemetry_lag_seconds) > 5

Circuit breaker open
- max by (region, hardware_class, pool) (redwood_burst_circuit_breaker_state{scope="pool"}) == 1

Denial reason composition (stacked)
- sum by (reason) (rate(redwood_burst_admission_decisions_total{decision="denied", region="$region", pool="$pool"}[10m]))


8) Instrumentation guidance (where to emit what)
Admission controller
- Emit admission_* metrics at the service boundary.
- Ensure every evaluation ends in exactly one decision counter increment.
- Map internal errors/timeouts into bounded reason + error_class labels.

Routing/gateway
- Emit routing_* metrics where “attempt” and “fallback” decisions happen.
- For retries: do not inflate “admission_requests_total” unless it is a true re-evaluation; ensure idempotency where possible.

Fleet / pool manager
- Emit pool_* gauges from the authoritative source of capacity (not from each worker).
- Ensure scrapes are stable even when pool is empty/unprovisioned (export 0s, don’t disappear series if possible).


9) Review checklist for adding a new burst metric
Before merging
- Does this metric duplicate an existing one with different naming?
- Is the label set bounded? (explicit list of allowed values)
- Does it introduce tenant_id/model_name/route_id style labels?
- Can the use-case be served by logs/traces instead?
- Are units and semantics documented?
- Is there a dashboard panel or alert planned? (avoid orphan metrics)

Owners for review
- Observability: Allison Grant / Sergio Costa
- SRE: Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes
- Platform (admission semantics): Ethan Park / Jordan Lee


10) Open questions (tracking)
- Do we need “queue” as a first-class decision, or do we always return immediate deny with client-side backoff? (impacts decision enum + queue metrics)
- Should “hardware_class” split between h100 and h100_mig (if MIG introduced later)? For now: no; treat as separate only if scheduling differs.
- What is the final tenant_tier taxonomy for GA contracts (gold/silver/standard vs enterprise/basic)? Need Product (Lauren/Chris) confirmation.

Change log (informal)
- 2025-02-05: initial draft created after architecture discussion; focused on naming + label ban list.
- 2025-03-07: added reason enum proposal + circuit breaker metrics.
- 2025-04-10: aligned with SLO-gate work and routing fallback metrics; tightened tenant label guidance.
